## About

The viewer styled with CSS. `css-class` adds a class to the viewer, and the
rules below use it to set the viewer's colors (plum, with pink links), draw a
line along the top of the caption band, and make the caption larger and italic.

```yaml
panzoom:
  css-class: plum-viewer
```

The rules apply only to a viewer with that class, so other pages keep the
default viewer even if they load the same rules. A single image or code cell can
add a class of its own, which applies while that image is open ([case 2](#c2)
and [case 4](#c4)).

The rules are in a raw HTML block on this page. The same block works in any
Quarto document:

````markdown {.show-source}
```{=html}
<style>
.plum-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9);
  --panzoom-bg: #2d1236;
  --panzoom-fg: #f3e8f7;
  --panzoom-link: #ffb3d9;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-footer {
  border-top: 4px solid #d58cf0;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-size: 1.15rem;
  font-style: italic;
}
.sea-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9);
  --panzoom-bg: #0f3640;
  --panzoom-fg: #e0f4f7;
  --panzoom-link: #7fe0d0;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-footer {
  border-top-color: #4fc3c9;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-style: normal;
}
</style>
```
````

The same rules can also go in a stylesheet file, or in the page's header:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    css: viewer.css   # a file holding the rules above
```

```yaml
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
        .plum-viewer { --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9); }
        </style>
```

A theme's `.scss` file works too. Rules on the viewer's parts start with the
viewer's class, as above, so they win over the defaults. The parts are
`.panzoom-footer` (the caption band), `.panzoom-caption`,
`.panzoom-description`, `.panzoom-hint`, `.panzoom-close`, `.panzoom-prev`,
`.panzoom-next`, and `.panzoom-counter`.

For a whole site, put `css-class` (or any option) under `format: html:` in
`_quarto.yml`. A top-level `panzoom:` there is replaced, not merged, by a page's
own `panzoom:` options.

## 1. Markdown image {#c1 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom`. It opens with the plum viewer from the rules
above, with a line along the top of the caption band and a larger, italic
caption, and the link in its caption is pink.

```markdown {.show-source}
![The Edgartown lighthouse, with a [link](https://quarto.org).](../../images/mv-2.jpg){.panzoom fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}
```

## 2. Class for one image {#c2 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom` and a class of its own,
`css-class="sea-viewer"`. It opens with the dark teal `.sea-viewer` rules, a
teal line along the top of the caption band, and an upright caption, and the
link in its caption is teal. The page's class stays on the viewer too, so the
`.sea-viewer` rules come after the `.plum-viewer` ones to win over them.

```markdown {.show-source}
![A gingerbread cottage, with a class of its own and a [link](https://quarto.org).](../../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom css-class="sea-viewer" fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}
```

## 3. Code cell {#c3 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

An R cell with `#| panzoom: true`. It opens with the plum viewer, as [case
1](#c1) does.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of vapor pressure rising steeply with temperature"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "Vapor pressure, from a cell with `panzoom: true`."

plot(pressure, type = "b", pch = 19)
```

## 4. Class for one cell {#c4 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

An R cell with `css-class: sea-viewer` under the `panzoom` cell option. It opens
with the teal viewer, as [case 2](#c2) does.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| panzoom:
#|   css-class: sea-viewer
#| fig-cap: "Stopping distance against speed, with a class of its own."

plot(cars, pch = 19)
```

## 5. Gallery with mixed classes {#c5 expect-open="panzoom" expect-steps="true"}

A gallery of three images, the first and last with `css-class="sea-viewer"`.
Each image has its class only while it is open, so the first and last show the
teal viewer and the middle one the plum viewer, whichever way it is reached.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Chilmark beach at sunset, with a class of its own.](../../images/mv-0.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" css-class="sea-viewer" fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)"}

![Aquinnah, with the class set on this page.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-no-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)"}

![A sailboat, with a class of its own.](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" css-class="sea-viewer" fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)"}
```
